base: A reconstruction-level classifier distinguishes data from simulated events and defines a likelihood-ratio weight.
The pairing of reconstructed and true events transfers that weight to truth, including unmatched events, and a truth-level classifier propagates a smooth reweighting to the next iteration.
We form cross sections by histogramming the reweighted truth events in the reporting binning and dividing by integrated flux, target count and bin width.
Events that fail reconstruction enter as unmatched truth events, so no separate efficiency correction is applied.
Backgrounds enter the reconstruction-level step through the density the classifier learns to match.

In the purity-based subtraction, every data event in reconstructed bin $b$ carries the weight $w_{\mathrm{pur}}(b)=\max(0,\,1-B_{b}/D_{b})$, where $D_{b}$ and $B_{b}$ are the data and predicted background counts in that bin, so the classifier's target density is $D(x)\,w_{\mathrm{pur}}(b)$.
The unbinned negative-weight treatment instead adds simulated background events with negative weight to the data, so that the target is $D(x)-B(x)$ pointwise.
A classifier refinement~\cite{StayPositive2025}, clipped at zero, converts the signed sample to non-negative weights before the first iteration.
The two targets share bin integrals wherever $B_{b}<D_{b}$ but differ inside a bin wherever the background fraction varies within it (\ssec{S4}{supp:estimators}).
With the refinement classifier, the negative-weight treatment removes most of the bias of purity-based subtraction at nominal truth in the highest-$W$ cells (\nsec{sec:val-negweight}).

Their step-1 weight comes from a regressor of that weight on the truth coordinates, fitted with equal event weights to the events that have a partner: it estimates the mean weight at fixed truth over simulated events, not over their physical weights.
These events carry \SIrange{\fvval{ess-nrp-min}}{\fvval{ess-nrp-max}}{\percent} of a cell's final weight (\ssecc{S4}{supp:estimators}).

The cross section in a bin of the observables $x_1,\dots,x_n$ is \begin{equation} \frac{d^{n}\sigma}{dx_{1}\cdots dx_{n}}=\frac{U}{c\,\Phi\,N_{\mathrm{T}}\,P\,\Delta x_{1}\cdots\Delta x_{n}}, \label{eq:xsec} \end{equation} with $U$ the unfolded yield, the sum of the final weights of the simulated truth events in the bin.
The completeness $c$ is the fraction of the bin's simulated truth-level signal that the unfolding input contains.

It is 1 in every bin, because every truth event without a reconstructed partner is appended to the input, and it is computed as a check (\nsec{sec:method-xsec}). $\Phi$ is the integrated flux per unit area and per proton on target, $N_{\mathrm{T}}$ the number of nucleons in the fiducial volume, $P$ the data exposure in protons on target, and $\Delta x_i$ the bin widths.
Backgrounds enter the reconstruction-level step through the density the classifier learns to match.

The change lowered $\chi^{2}/\mathrm{ndf}$ from $\chiPaperPurity$ to $\chiPaper$ (\ssec{S4}{supp:estimators}).
That comparison is therefore conditional on both choices.

In the weight universes, every simulated event's truth and reconstructed weights, and the truth denominator, take the universe's values, so the events without a reconstructed partner carry their universe weights too (\ssec{S5}{supp:cov16}).

base: \label{supp:study-band} \label{sec:coverage} This test asks whether a 2D statistical band covers a \emph{fixed} truth at its nominal rate.
The test evaluated the \emph{completeness-divided band}, the initial statistical band quoted when the test ran, whose replicas divide by a bootstrapped completeness.
The \emph{undivided band} is the rebuilt band, without the division, since superseded.
The quoted statistical block (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:uq-boot}) is a separate ensemble of 300 replicas at the central value's training seed.
The design, criteria and positive control of the test were specified before any toy was generated (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:coverage}).
Each toy draws pseudo-data event by event as Poisson counts with means equal to the simulated reconstructed weights.

It resamples the simulation with the per-event Poisson(1) bootstrap of the statistical band and unfolds with that band's estimator, LightGBM with five iterations at a fixed training seed, the learner of the quoted central value at a different seed (Sec.~\ref{sec:method-config}).
The reference $T$ is the unfluctuated simulated truth, identical in every toy.
The no-fluctuation configuration reproduces both the production closure output and $T$ exactly.
In reported bin $b$ of toy $t$, $z_{tb}=(U_{tb}-T_b)/(r_b T_b)$, where $r_b$ is the production band's relative spread.
Coverage $C_k$ is the fraction of all (toy, bin) pairs with $|z|\le k$, with intervals from resampling whole toys.

The band is considered nominal if its ratio to the true scatter lies in $[0.9,1.1]$, which gives the windows $C_1\in[\covTwoDWinOneLo,\covTwoDWinOneHi]$ and $C_2\in[\covTwoDWinTwoLo,\covTwoDWinTwoHi]$.
A failure at the interim analysis of 100 toys, with 99.5\% intervals, stops the study.
\textbf{Scope.} The test concerns the statistical band alone and changes no central value or quoted uncertainty.
It tests the LightGBM statistical estimator at the band's training seed (seed~1); the quoted central value uses seed~42, and the test does not address systematic, total or five-dimensional coverage.
Its simulation-side scatter reuses the resampling that built the band, so only the data-side fluctuation is tested by an independent mechanism.
Because $T$ equals the prior, the test cannot detect regularization bias toward the prior.
